Parent: [#402](https://github.com/brianreborn/familia/issues/402) (Security focus for 0.3.0). Target: `main`. Unassigned so the swarm can claim. Suggested owners: Boundary Reviewer (tool policy, including residual TR-3/TR-4), Covert Channel Reviewer/Fixer (injection via tool results, egress), Platform Reviewer (inventory of what is actually wired).

## Context

What familia wires today (inventory starting point, not complete):

- Agent-Reach: menu `reach.mcp` runs `scripts/agent_reach.py mcp-example` and prints `mcpServers` JSON for llama UI / code-bootstraps.
- Hermes / graph: `scripts/hermes_harness.py`, `server_tools` on nodes. Some planned nodes use `server_tools: all`; guardian/pentest nodes stay empty (TOOLS-005 fail-closed). DESIGN.md: the existing approval gate still guards shell and MCP.
- Auth env: `API_KEY_FILE`, `FAMILIA_API_KEY`, `LLAMA_API_KEY` (see `docs/api-key-design.md`, `scripts/familia_auth.py`). #394 is a test KeyError on `GITHUB_TOKEN` under FreeBSD.
- Already fixed, do not re-open as new bugs: H4 (read-only tools by default after #292), #345 (off-loopback direct tools; closed).

Residual product gaps with tests already on `main` (strict xfails in `tests/test_routing_toolroute_boundary.py` after #364 / [#362](https://github.com/brianreborn/familia/pull/362)). No public issue had been filed for these, so they live here rather than as a fifth tracker:

- TR-3 residual: `normalize_role` does NFKC + casefold but does not `strip()` or drop Unicode format characters (category Cf, e.g. U+200B). Padded or lookalike fail-closed role names (`guardian` / `pentest` / `defender`) become unknown TYPEs, so tools can be forwarded. Case and fullwidth variants were already tightened in #362.
- TR-4: a node-level `role: coder` (or other tool-capable type) can override a fail-closed model role, so a guardian model can be relabelled into a tool-forward path.

Related: green-roomz #43 (default-deny egress, research only), #236 leftover L14/L15.

opportunities.title: [Security][MCP][P0] Restrict local HTTP MCP access to trusted origins and safe bind addresses
opportunities.excerpt:
## Security problem

The local MCP HTTP transport in `internal/mcp/http.go` sets `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *` on both SSE and message endpoints. The message endpoint also allows cross-origin `POST` requests with `Content-Type`, and the local server does not authenticate callers or validate browser origins.

The CLI defaults to `127.0.0.1`, which is a good starting point, but `krew mcp --host` accepts a caller-supplied bind address and does not require authentication when binding beyond loopback.

This is a sensitive boundary because the local MCP tools can inspect project metadata, create files through scaffolding, run the project's Go tests, and execute verification commands. A hostile website may be able to issue cross-origin requests to a local instance; a non-loopback bind can expose the same capabilities to other network clients.

## Required work

- Remove wildcard CORS for the privileged local MCP transport.
- Validate `Origin` against an explicit configurable allowlist for supported IDE/client origins.
- Validate the HTTP `Host` header and reject unexpected hosts to reduce DNS-rebinding exposure.
- Preserve native STDIO clients and document the behavior for requests without an `Origin` header.
- Keep loopback binding as the secure default.
- Refuse non-loopback binding unless an explicit authentication mechanism and secure configuration are provided.
- Add a per-instance capability token or equivalent protection for HTTP mode; do not expose secrets in URLs or logs.
- Add rate limiting or equivalent abuse controls for tool execution endpoints.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] No privileged local MCP endpoint responds with wildcard CORS.
- [ ] Requests from untrusted browser origins are rejected before tool execution.
- [ ] Allowed IDE origins can complete the MCP handshake and tool calls.
- [ ] Unexpected Host headers are rejected.
- [ ] Loopback remains the default bind address.
- [ ] Non-loopback binding requires explicit secure authentication configuration and produces a clear warning.
- [ ] Tests prove that an untrusted origin cannot read project information, scaffold files, or trigger test execution.
- [ ] Native STDIO operation is unaffected.
- [ ] Security behavior and configuration are documented.

## Priority

P0 — the local MCP server exposes project inspection and execution capabilities and must have a defensible browser/network trust bou

opportunities.title: Security: bump Node base image and dependencies in backend and mcp-server (multer, nodemailer, body-parser, ...)
opportunities.excerpt:
Found by a scheduled Trivy scan (v0.76.2, DB of 2026-11-23) of the published `backend` and `mcp-server` images. Risk is rated by whether the code actually reaches the vulnerable path.

## Risk: MEDIUM — worth doing soon

| Package | Image | Fixed in | Why it matters here |
|---|---|---|---|
| multer 1.4.5-lts.1 (via `@nestjs/platform-express` 11.0.1) | backend | 2.3.0 | 10 denial-of-service advisories on multipart parsing. Used by `POST /scraper/import/upload` and the plugin upload. Both are behind `JwtAuthGuard`, so only a logged-in user can trigger them. Fix: bump `@nestjs/platform-express` to a current 11.x. |
| nodemailer 8.0.1 | backend | 8.0.8 (9.x/10.x for all) | CVE-2026-82662 TLS certificate verification disabled in some paths (info disclosure of SMTP traffic); addressparser ReDoS. Used in `push.service.ts`. |
| body-parser 1.20.3 / 2.2.1 | both | 1.20.9 / 2.4.0 | CVE-2026-111181 DoS via decompression stream error, reachable before auth on any JSON endpoint that accepts a compressed body. |
| hono 4.11.4, @hono/node-server 1.19.9 (via `@modelcontextprotocol/node`) | mcp-server | 4.12.25 / 1.19.10 | serveStatic file access and CORS origin reflection. Low unless serveStatic or hono's CORS middleware is used; bump with the MCP packages anyway. |
| joi 18.0.2 | backend | 18.3.1 | ReDoS in email / isoDate validation if user input goes through those rules. |
| adm-zip 0.5.16 | backend | 0.6.1 | DoS / zip-bomb and permission bits on extract. Admin-only plugin upload; path traversal is already guarded. |

## Risk: LOW — not reachable in practice, cleared by the same rebuild

| Package | Fixed in | Why low |
|---|---|---|
| **proxy-addr 2.0.7** (critical, CVE-2026-90711) | 2.0.8 | Only matters with `trust proxy` set to subnets; neither app sets `trust proxy`. |
| **OpenSSL 3.5.5** (critical, CVE-2026-31789) | 3.5.6+ | Heap overflow on 32-bit systems only; plus 6 high (DoS, one use-after-free in CMS/PKCS7). Cleared by a newer `node:24-alpine` base. |
| **tar 7.5.1** (critical, CVE-2026-59873) + pacote, sigstore, glob, minimatch, brace-expansion | — | Inside npm's own bundled copy in the base image; npm is not run at runtime. |
| mysql2, hono, effect, defu, deepmerge-ts, lodash | — | Pulled in by prisma / build tooling; not used at runtime with PostgreSQL. |
| path-to-regexp 8.2.0 | 8.4.0 | ReDoS only with crafted *route definitions*, which are ours. |

opportunities.title: Sample hooks: ask the graph what an edit reached (Claude Code and Kiro)
opportunities.excerpt:
## What

Ship sample hooks that ask the DeepMorph MCP server what an edit reached, right after a coding agent changes files. One sample for Claude Code, one for Kiro.

Today the plugin is pulled: an agent runs `/deepmorph:map` before it starts a task. Nothing asks the graph again after the agent has edited code. A hook would push the same graph context at the point where an edit can still be corrected.

## Why a hook

Kiro documents this pattern for another MCP server. Its hook examples include one that fires on **File Save** for `*.css` and `*.html` and tells the agent to "Use the Figma MCP to analyze the updated html or css files and check that they follow established design patterns in the figma design" (https://kiro.dev/docs/hooks/examples.md). Kiro also has a **Post Task Execution** trigger, which fires after a spec task completes (https://kiro.dev/docs/hooks/types.md). Claude Code has `PostToolUse` and `Stop` hooks that fit the same place.

## Scope

- A Claude Code hook in the plugin, off by default: on `Stop` (or `PostToolUse` for file edits), an agent prompt that passes the changed paths to the MCP server and asks which business scenarios, UI surfaces and data lifecycle edges they reach, then reports what the edit may have affected.
- A Kiro hook file in the README, for **Post Task Execution** or **File Save** with a narrow file pattern, doing the same through the same MCP server.
- Narrow triggers. Kiro's own advice is to "Use specific file glob patterns" and to keep hook prompts short.

## Not in scope

No new MCP tool. The samples use only the tools the server already exposes.

## Open questions

- `Stop` or `PostToolUse`: once per turn is cheaper; per edit is earlier.
- Whether the hook should only report, or also ask the agent to re-check the reached scenarios before finishing.
